BLOCKING_FINDING.claim: element.imports[].specifiers is DEAD DATA. It is declared, always emitted as [], and never populated for TypeScript. Same for .default and .namespace.
BLOCKING_FINDING.measured: 26 of 26 import entries across 4 importing files carried specifiers: [], default: absent, namespace: absent - including files whose source plainly contains `import { X } from ...`.
BLOCKING_FINDING.proof: Grammar-level probe on the identical 3-line source. `node.childForFieldName("import_clause")` returns NULL for all three import forms; `node.namedChildren.find(c => c.type === "import_clause")` returns the import_clause node. relationship-extractor.ts:1106 uses the FORMER, so the entire specifiers/default/namespace block at :1120-1144 is UNREACHABLE for TypeScript. Legacy extractImports returned {sourceFile,target,line} only; extractRawImports on the SAME source returned specifiers [alpha,beta], defaultImport Def, namespaceImport NS, plus typeOnly.
BLOCKING_FINDING.the_defect_class_again: TWO import extractors in ONE class. The raw-facts path at :467 carries a comment stating "tree-sitter-typescript exposes `import_clause` as an unnamed-field child rather than via childForFieldName, so look it up by type." That fix was never backported to the legacy path 640 lines below it. This is the THIRD instance of the same class in this codebase - two components disagreeing about one seam, one fixed and one not, with nothing testing the seam.
BLOCKING_FINDING.blast_radius_today: LOW and measured: NO consumer of element.imports reads .specifiers. Every `specifiers` reference in src/ outside the extractor is the separate Acorn-based js-call-detector (which populates its own) or a type declaration. The dead field currently harms nothing.
BLOCKING_FINDING.why_it_BLOCKS_this_phase: P1-T3 planned to narrow element.imports to the imports an element actually references. That rule needs specifier / default / namespace tokens to match against the element body. Those tokens do not exist in the data the scanner path produces. The plan assumed a field that is structurally empty.

consumers_verified_first_hand: src/query/clones.ts:247 (isTrivial) and :382 (clone signature) - reads source only
COUNT: 7 read sites across 7 modules. The source comment at tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:99 claimed "six consumers" - close, and now verified rather than repeated. NONE of them reads .specifiers.
extractImports_callers: src/pipeline/orchestrator.ts:462 - and :465 calls extractRawImports on the SAME node, so the orchestrator already computes the CORRECT data alongside the broken data. Same shape as the ctx.calls finding: a legacy seed layer beside a correct canonical one.

narrowing_rule_ruled.rule: An import is retained on an element when ANY of its bound local names (named specifiers, default, namespace alias) appears as a whole word in the element body span [line, endLine].
narrowing_rule_ruled.conservative_by_design: Keep-on-any-match. The two error directions are NOT symmetric: a false KEEP retains an unused import (harmless, and it is the status quo), while a false DROP discards an import the element genuinely uses (data loss). The rule therefore errs toward keeping.
narrowing_rule_ruled.known_limits: This is a TEXT heuristic, not symbol resolution. A name appearing only in a comment or string keeps its import; a symbol reached dynamically or by computed access may be dropped. Real resolution needs the symbol table, which is far larger than this phase. Recorded so no reader mistakes the heuristic for precision.
narrowing_rule_ruled.operator_accepted_tradeoff: Occasional retained-but-unused import, in exchange for fixing the measured 193-vs-1264 clones.ts triviality understatement.

After narrowing it is per-element, so clone GROUPING changes, not just the triviality flag at :247.

tasks.description: MEASURE that the inline predicate at src/cli/rag-search.ts:313-315 and the canonical isLocalOnly() at src/integration/rag/rag-config.ts:144-149 really are behaviourally identical, across the FULL input matrix (unset, empty, 0, false, no, and their case variants, plus 1/true/yes/off/arbitrary). AUDIT reachability AND testability of the seam, before editing. Two questions, both answered first-hand: (1) is the rag-search guard live - is rag-search a real bin, is main() reachable, does anything spawn it; (2) after the collapse, can any test reach the guard. HALT AND REPORT with named options if P2-T2 shows the collapsed guard cannot be reached by a test. P2_T1_predicate_equivalence.method: Differential probe. BOTH predicates transcribed verbatim from source (rag-search.ts:313-315 and rag-config.ts:144-149) and run over a 22-case input matrix: unset, empty, 0/false/no and their case variants, 1/true/TRUE/yes, and the awkward ones - "off", "disabled", "-1", "00", " ", "0 ", " 0", "null". Transcribed rather than imported so the comparison is of the two SHAPES, independent of module wiring.
P2_T1_predicate_equivalence.return_type_differences: 2 of 22 - for unset the inline form yields undefined and for "" it yields "", where the canonical returns a strict false. Both are falsy and the value is consumed ONLY as `if (localOnly && ...)`, so the guard cannot observe the difference. The collapse actually tightens the type.
P2_T1_predicate_equivalence.verdict: CONFIRMED behaviourally identical. The predecessor workorder claim is re-verified independently rather than inherited.
P2_T1_predicate_equivalence.incidental_finding_NOT_fixed: Both predicates treat "off", "disabled", "-1" and " " as local-only ENABLED - only 0/false/no disable it. That is surprising, but it is SHARED by both sides, so the collapse does not change it and fixing it would be a behaviour change smuggled in under a refactor. It also errs toward local-only, which is the safe direction in an environment with no cloud LLM keys.

P2_T2_reachability_and_testability.is_the_guard_live: YES. rag-search is a published bin (package.json "rag-search" -> dist/src/cli/rag-search.js) and main() runs on every invocation. Nothing in-repo SPAWNS it - every in-repo "rag-search" hit is a comment, a docstring or a @used_by line - so its only caller is a human or an external script. Live, not dead.
P2_T2_reachability_and_testability.can_a_test_reach_it: NO, not today. src/cli/rag-search.ts has ZERO exports and calls main() unconditionally at module tail. Importing it from a test would parse process.argv and process.exit() the test runner.
P2_T2_reachability_and_testability.sibling_comparison: rag-index.ts, rag-status.ts and rag-eval.ts ALL guard main() behind `require.main === module` and export their surface (rag-index: parseArgs, runRagIndex, defaultRagIndexArgs, +2 types). rag-search is the ONLY member of the four-CLI rag-* family without the guard.
P2_T2_reachability_and_testability.repo_wide_census: 5 of 23 non-test files in src/cli/ carry a require.main guard (coderef-mcp-server, populate, rag-eval, rag-index, rag-status). So the guard is NOT a repo-wide norm - but it IS the norm for the rag-* family, which is the family this seam lives in. Measured rather than asserted, because "everyone does it" and "its own siblings do it" are different arguments and only the second is true.
P2_T2_reachability_and_testability.the_finding: This is why the predicate could be copied four times. rag-search is STRUCTURALLY UNTESTABLE, so every previous attempt to pin the local-only contract had to assert a private copy of the predicate instead of the CLI that uses it. Collapsing onto isLocalOnly() removes the copy but does NOT make the seam provable - a test could still only assert isLocalOnly() in isolation, which is exactly the shape the predecessor workorder had to delete from the rag-index test.

testability_ruling_P2_T3.ruling: (A) collapse AND mirror the sibling convention
testability_ruling_P2_T3.why_a_ruling_was_needed: The collapse alone is safe and proven identical, but rag-search.ts had zero exports and ran main() at import, so nothing could test the collapsed guard. Making a module testable changes its module contract, which is beyond the stub scope and therefore the operator call - the same halt shape that fired at P1-T3.
testability_ruling_P2_T3.what_it_authorises: Guard main() behind require.main === module and export the guard as assertLocalOnlyAllows(provider) so a test drives the real decision.
